objective: Give the mesh standard the generator-selection rule its evidence already supports: a refinement-trend criterion on worst-cell quality, the measured twin-generator comparison as its warrant, and a disposition for every mesh still outside the birth-certificate population so the certificate claim becomes universal rather than nearly universal
rationale: Both halves of this proof are one step from done and neither step has been taken. The evidence half is complete and unusually clean, because the comparison was a controlled twin: at matched cell counts of 4,032 and 14,720, the identical user-facing refinement moves that worsen the hyperbolic generator's worst cell by a factor of 1.711 improve the structured C-grid's by a factor of 0.945, and within one chord of the wall the alternative sits at 37.4 against the reference family's 87.6. The verdict rule was frozen before any mesh existed, the generator-owned threshold was pre-declared at 1.0 and the recipe-owned threshold at 1.3, and the whole matrix cost about 0.4 core-minutes of the roughly 20 approved. The same campaign produced a result that should be quoted rather than buried: the standard's own entry gate refused the alternative mesh's smoke solve on the standard's second day, because its non-orthogonality read 70.11 degrees against a 70 degree hard bar, 0.16 percent over, and it refused against its own author's arm with no post-hoc tuning. The tip-collapse question is characterised too: the collapse appears once, on a four-times-coarsened wing tip, as 25 cells at an aspect ratio near 2.08e+95 with 23 negative-volume cells clustered at the tip trailing-edge corner, while every other reachable mesh from the same generator is born clean and the same family is pinned at 608.2 across its usable range. What the standard does not have is a rule. Version 1.1 states in its own opening that it adds exactly one mechanism and changes no gate value, and the word generator appears in it only as a certificate field and a descriptive aside, so nothing in it says which generator to prefer, or that a worsening worst-cell trend under refinement is itself a signal. The cross-check that keeps the rule honest is also on the record: reference C-grids from the benchmark family worsen far more strongly under refinement, and their extreme cells sit hundreds of chords downstream in the wake cut, so a naive trend gate would condemn meshes the lab has no business condemning and the rule must be banded near the wall. On the certificate half, the sweep reached 178 unique meshes from 873 case-level instances and certified them, leaving a named remainder: derived points-only snapshots, a high-aspect-ratio flag-only class, and 41 case meshes referenced by records but no longer on disk, 38 of them with retained certificates. Universal means those are dispositioned, not ignored. Axis A: report-kind at zero solver cost. Axis B: 0, it changes no wall row directly, though it gates what may become one. Axis C: 0.

cost_basis: measured; the twin-generator matrix that supplies the evidence is already spent at about 0.4 core-min and the archive sweep at about 1.4 core-min, so absorbing them into the standard and dispositioning the certificate remainder is a text and bookkeeping pass with no solver time and no case opened
expected_knowledge_gain: The standard either gains a rule that would have caught the pathology before a mesh was solved on, or the attempt shows the rule cannot be written without condemning good meshes, and that is a finding about the metric rather than about the generator. Concretely, the near-wall banding is the test: if a worst-cell trend criterion restricted to the near-wall band separates the pathological family from the reference family, the rule is writable and the evidence supports it; if it does not, the honest outcome is that generator selection stays advisory and the standard says so instead of implying a rule it cannot enforce. The certificate half returns a number, the count of meshes still outside the population and the disposition of each class, which converts a nearly-universal claim into an exact one.
sequencing: Dispatchable now. Strategy rule 4 ride-along with no new compute; the generator-parameter ablation that would confirm the mechanism is named as a follow-on rather than folded in, because the generator is not installed on the host that measured the matrix.
gate: STRATEGY PROOF CLAUSE, verbatim: 'Mesh generation science: pyHyp pathology characterized (when does tip collapse occur) + alternative-generator matrix -> PROOF: MESH_STANDARD gains a generator-selection rule with evidence; birth certificates universal.' Operationalised in three parts, all required. (a) The standard gains a numbered generator-selection clause carrying the measured twin comparison as its warrant, stating the worst-cell refinement-trend criterion, banding it to the near-wall region so the reference-family wake cut does not trip it, and stating whether the clause is a hard gate or advisory. (b) The tip-collapse characterisation enters as a stated condition rather than an anecdote, naming the coarsening regime and the surface geometry under which it occurs and what a certificate would show. (c) Every mesh outside the certified population is dispositioned by class, with a count per class and a stated rule for the referenced-but-absent case, so the universality claim is exact. A clause that states a preference without the trend criterion, or a universality claim with an undispositioned remainder, fails.
